attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, written in his voice.

semantics.note: The sentence is a call to action, but its relative clause makes a factual claim: the companies spend far more than they earn. Treating that clause as an observation is fair. The opinion words are kept but not scored.

contract.note: Scoring only the checkable core (spending versus revenue), with OpenAI as the main referent and 2025 data before the post, is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Far more' is tested as costs or losses clearly above revenue.

evidence.note: H1 2025 revenue of about $4.3B, from Reuters relaying shareholder disclosures. This is the revenue side of the comparison.
R&D alone was $6.7B in H1 2025, about 1.6 times revenue for the same period.
From Microsoft's equity-method loss, OpenAI lost an implied ~$11.5B in Q3 2025. That is a derived estimate, but it points to losses far above revenue.
The reporter's own side-by-side of the loss and revenue. It is commentary that adds no new outcome data.
Anthropic: a different company, full-year figures, published later. Context only.

reviews.rationale: Reliable reports before the post show OpenAI's 2025 R&D costs ($6.7B in H1) well above its revenue ($4.3B in H1), plus an implied Q3 loss of about $11.5B. Spending was far above revenue, not marginally above it. The opinion words were not scored.

attribution.note: The figures come from Gerstner's question, but Marcus repeats them as fact ('a mere $13 billion'), so he adopts them.

semantics.note: The proposition correctly sets aside the narration of Altman's mood and keeps the two figures being compared.

contract.note: The speaker named no revenue basis. In Nov 2025 an informed reader would take $13B as OpenAI's expected 2025 revenue. That basis is identifiable, so the contract can be met without stretching it either way.

evidence.note: Altman said OpenAI committed to 30GW, a $1.4T obligation over a few years. This is a company statement, but it matches the contract's definition of announced commitments.
Reuters: OpenAI's full-year 2025 revenue target was $13B. That gives an identifiable basis for the $13B figure. It is a projection, not realized revenue.

reviews.rationale: Both figures match contemporaneous records: about $1.4T in announced multiyear infrastructure commitments (Altman's statement) and $13B as OpenAI's 2025 full-year revenue target. The basis is a projection, not realized revenue, but nothing shows a materially different figure.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Which means' follows from the government going along, so the antecedent is kept correctly. The consequent 'will' is firm. 'AI companies' slightly widens a context centred on OpenAI.

contract.note: Requiring documented adoption, then a realized cost or a final settlement, is a reasonable reading of 'footing the bill'. Counting only contingent exposure would be an alternative reading.

evidence.note: A GSA procurement deal for ChatGPT access. It is not a financing backstop, so it neither meets the antecedent nor settles the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent (the government adopting a backstop for AI company borrowing) is not shown in the evidence by the evaluation date. No deadline was stated. A conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical aside in his post.

semantics.note: 'Seems intent' hedges both how things appear and what Nvidia intends. The proposition keeps that hedge ('appears'), which takes it out of scoring.

contract.note: The contract applies a plain reading and scores a hedged statement. Under the policy, plain reading applies only to firm language. 'The same play' is also undefined and had to be supplied by the evaluator.

evidence.note: Huang's China-competition and energy remarks. They do not show a request for financing backing, so this is context only.

reviews.rationale: 'Seems intent' is a hedge about Nvidia's apparent intent, and 'the same play' is unspecified. Hedged language like this is not scored under the policy. The evidence would not settle it in any case.
